written.q: What is Network Functions Virtualization? State four advantages. (6 marks)
written.a: NFV decouples network functions such as firewalls, routers and encryption from dedicated proprietary hardware and runs them as software on virtual machines on standard commodity servers, reducing cost and accelerating service deployment; a new function is added by spinning up a VM. Advantages: reduced space for network hardware, reduced power consumption, reduced maintenance and hardware costs, easier upgrades, longer hardware life cycles, management from anywhere in the operator's network.

NFV virtualizes individual network functions (they become software on VMs instead of appliances). SDN separates the control plane from the data plane and centralizes control in a software controller that programs the forwarding devices. They are complementary: SDN can steer traffic between virtualized functions.

written.q: Explain the "works on my machine" problem and how containers solve it. (4)
written.a: Software works on the developer's machine but fails elsewhere because of different library versions, configurations or OS settings (dependency conflicts, inconsistent environments). A container packages the application with all its dependencies into an image, so the same image runs identically in development, testing and production.

written.q: Describe the Docker architecture. Distinguish an image from a container. (6)
written.a: Docker uses a client-server model: the client sends commands (build, run, pull) to the Docker daemon, which builds images, runs containers, and manages networks, volumes and communication with registries. Registries (e.g. Docker Hub) store and share images. An image is a read-only template built from a Dockerfile in layers; a container is a running instance created from an image, and many containers can be created from one image.

written.q: Why is data stored in volumes rather than inside containers? (2)
written.a: Containers are ephemeral; when one is removed its internal file system is lost. Volumes store data outside the container so it persists across container removal and replacement.

written.q: Draw and explain a highly available web architecture on AWS. (8)
written.a: (Draw Figure 4.) A VPC spans two AZs. Each AZ has a public subnet with a NAT gateway and a private subnet with web front-end and app servers. An Application Load Balancer distributes requests across both AZs. The web and app tiers are in Auto Scaling groups spanning both AZs, which replace unhealthy instances and scale with demand. RDS runs a primary in AZ1 replicated to a secondary in AZ2. No tier has a single point of failure; losing an entire AZ still leaves a working copy.

written.q: Compare target tracking, simple and step scaling policies. (6)
written.a: Target tracking keeps a metric at a target value (e.g. CPU 50%), adding or removing instances automatically. Simple scaling performs one fixed action when a CloudWatch alarm fires (e.g. +1 instance at CPU > 70%). Step scaling uses banded ranges: the larger the breach, the larger the adjustment.

RTO (recovery time objective) is the maximum acceptable downtime before service is restored. RPO (recovery point objective) is the maximum acceptable data loss, measured as the time between the last recoverable copy and the disaster.

Backup & restore: only scheduled backups copied across regions, no standby; infrastructure built after the event; RPO/RTO hours; lowest cost. Pilot light: data replicated live, app tier idle; servers provisioned after the event; tens of minutes; low-medium cost. Warm standby: a scaled-down fully working copy always running; scaled up after the event; minutes; higher cost. Multi-site active/active: full production in both sites serving traffic; real-time recovery with near-zero data loss; highest cost.

written.q: Compare horizontal and vertical scaling with examples. (4)
written.a: Horizontal scaling adds or removes instances (scale out: 2 → 6 servers; scale in when demand drops); it improves availability. Vertical scaling makes one instance more powerful (c3.large → c4.8xlarge, scale up); it has an upper limit and usually needs a restart.

written.q: Give two advantages of RDS over running a database on EC2, and one reason to choose EC2. (3)
written.a: RDS: AWS handles patching and maintenance; automated backups with point-in-time recovery and Multi-AZ failover. EC2: full shell access to the server and its dependencies, and lower usage cost if you accept the DBA work.
